voicemail_transcript.text: Yeah hi, this is Marisol, I live at 2204 Kettle Street, apartment 3. Um, there's this car, a silver Honda I think, maybe a Civic, that's been sitting in the parking lot behind the Suds-N-Go laundromat for like three weeks now. It's got two flat tires and somebody smashed the back window and now there's glass everywhere and kids cut through there to get to the school. The plate starts with 7K something, I couldn't see the rest because it's bent. It's kind of half in the lot, half hanging over into the alley, I really can't tell where the lot ends. The laundromat guy says it's not one of his customers. Can someone come tow it? My number is 555-0139. Thanks.

kb_routing_articles.KB-101 Abandoned vehicle on public stree: Vehicles parked on a public street or alley for more than 72 hours, or inoperable on the public right-of-way, go to Parking Enforcement (Abandoned Vehicle Unit). Staff will tag and tow after the notice period.
kb_routing_articles.KB-102 Abandoned or junk vehicle on priv: Inoperable, wrecked or unregistered vehicles on private property (including business parking lots) are handled by Code Enforcement under the Property Maintenance Code; the property owner is cited. The city does not tow from private property without owner consent or a code order.
kb_routing_articles.KB-103 Vehicle blocking driveway: Route to Police Non-Emergency for immediate response.
kb_routing_articles.KB-117 Broken glass or debris in the pub: Street Maintenance sweeps glass and debris from streets, alleys and sidewalks. Glass on private lots is the owner's responsibility.
kb_routing_articles.KB-140 Stolen vehicle suspicion: If the caller believes the vehicle is stolen, advise them to call Police Non-Emergency; 311 also creates a courtesy ticket for Police.
kb_routing_articles.KB-208 Laundromat and dry-cleaning licen: Business license questions for coin laundries go to Business Licensing.
kb_routing_articles.KB-311 Straddling locations: When an item straddles private property and the public right-of-way, route by where the greater part of the item sits; if that is unclear, route to the department responsible for the private-property portion and copy the department responsible for the public portion.

service.note: The car is 'half in the lot, half over the alley' and the caller can't tell which part is bigger, so KB-311 routes to the private-property department (Code Enforcement, KB-102) and copies the public one.

copy_department.note: The public portion of the car is in the alley (Parking Enforcement, KB-101), but the glass the kids walk through may be in the alley too (Street Maintenance, KB-117); which public-side department to copy is a close call.

glass_public.note: 'Glass everywhere' around a car that straddles the lot and alley, where kids cut through, could put glass in the alley, but the caller never says where the glass lies relative to the lot line.

urgency.note: Broken glass where schoolchildren cut through is a specific risk to children (Priority), but no one is hurt and the car has sat for weeks, so many would call it an elevated nuisance.

program_manual.CCAP 2.1 Activity requirement: Each parent in the household must be employed, in an approved education or training program, or searching for work (job search is limited to 12 weeks per year). The activity must be verified before approval.
program_manual.CCAP 2.4 Exemption - homelessness: Families experiencing homelessness are exempt from the activity requirement for an initial 3-month eligibility period. Homelessness may be verified by a shelter letter, a school McKinney-Vento liaison letter, or caseworker observation documented in the file. Families living doubled-up with others due to loss of housing meet the definition.
program_manual.CCAP 2.6 Child age: Children must be under 13, or under 19 with a documented special need.
program_manual.CCAP 3.2 Income: Household income must be at or below the limit; income is verified by the eligibility system (field income_test).
program_manual.CCAP 4.1 Priority groups: Priority is given to teen parents, families receiving TANF, and families experiencing homelessness.
program_manual.CCAP 5.3 Copayment: Families approved under 2.4 pay the minimum copayment during the initial period.
program_manual.CCAP 6.1 Providers: Care must be provided by a licensed center, a licensed family home, or a registered license-exempt relative provider.
program_manual.CCAP 7.2 Reporting changes: Families must report a new address, a change in household members or a new job to their worker. Reports may be made by phone, portal or in person.
program_manual.CCAP 8.1 Fair hearings: An applicant may request a fair hearing on any denial, reduction or delay in processing.

request.text: I'm requesting the body-worn camera video from the two officers who stopped me on March 14 on Route 9 near the Gas-N-Go (incident 26-031477). I was the driver. I want to see the whole thing including when they searched my car. My passenger that night was my cousin, she's fine with it being released too. Please send it on a USB drive, I don't have good internet.

records_policy.BWC-1: Body-worn camera recordings are public records subject to the exemptions below.
records_policy.BWC-2 Active investigation: A recording may be withheld while it relates to an open criminal investigation or prosecution, if release would reasonably be expected to interfere with it. Once the matter is closed with no charges, or adjudicated, this exemption no longer applies.
records_policy.BWC-3 Subject access: A person who is the subject of a recording, or their attorney, may obtain an unredacted copy of the portions depicting them, except where BWC-2 applies.
records_policy.BWC-4 Privacy redactions: Faces and identifying details of bystanders, minors, victims and witnesses, and of any other person who is not the requesting subject, must be redacted before release. Portions showing the interior of a private residence are redacted unless the resident consents.
records_policy.BWC-5 Third-party consent: A person depicted may waive redaction of themselves only by written, signed consent.
records_policy.BWC-6 Format and fees: Recordings are provided as MP4 on physical media at a $10 media fee or by secure download at no charge. Redaction time is billed at the clerk hourly rate after the first hour.
records_policy.BWC-7 Retention: Non-evidentiary recordings are retained 190 days; recordings tagged to an incident are retained until the case closes plus 3 years.

Incident 26-031477: CLOSED - lab negative; no charges filed. Closed by Det. Imani Rowe.

criteria.release_unredacted_full: Release both videos with no redactions
criteria.release_with_redactions: Release, redacting people other than the requester

redaction_burden.instructions: How much redaction work does the located footage require before release to the requester?

criteria.definition: Only the requester appears
A single other person, or brief appearances

bwc2_applies.note: The 04-03 entry was OPEN, but the 05-21 entry closes the case with no charges, and BWC-2 ends at closure.

requester_is_subject.note: He was the driver who was stopped.

passenger_redaction.note: BWC-4 requires redacting anyone other than the requesting subject, and BWC-5 needs written signed consent; the requester only says his cousin is 'fine with it', which is not written consent. Some reviewers would accept it pending a form.

release_decision.note: BWC-2 no longer applies after closure; the subject gets his own portions, but the two bystanders must be redacted in any case, so an unredacted full release isn't supported.

redaction_burden.note: The passenger appears in both videos and two bystanders in one, with no minors or interiors: several people across both, which is moderate.

We want to put up lit channel letters above the door (about 8 ft wide); our electrician will connect it to the existing circuit. We'd also like to hang a grand opening banner for about two weeks. permit_catalog.BL Business License: Required to operate any business; apply before opening. Annual renewal each January.
permit_catalog.SP Sign Permit: All permanent signs attached to a building or freestanding. Submit dimensions, mounting detail and a scaled elevation drawing. Typical review is two weeks.
permit_catalog.EP Electrical Permit: Required for any new wiring or connection, including illuminated signs. Must be pulled by a licensed electrician.
permit_catalog.COA Certificate of Appropriateness: Required BEFORE any other permit for exterior changes, including signs, in the Old Town Historic District (100-400 blocks of Front St and Mill St). Reviewed by the Historic Commission at its monthly meeting; applications close three weeks before the meeting.
permit_catalog.TSP Temporary Sign Permit: Banners and temporary signs displayed up to 30 days. No drawings required; a sketch and dates suffice.
permit_catalog.ZV Zoning Variance: Only when a proposal exceeds zoning limits; sign area limits are in Zoning Code 19.40.
permit_catalog.BP Building Permit: Structural work; not required for signs under 50 sq ft mounted flush to a wall.
permit_catalog.ROW Right-of-Way Permit: Anything projecting over the public sidewalk more than 12 inches, including blade signs and awnings.
permit_catalog.HP Health Permit: Food service establishments, issued by the County Health Department, not the city.
permit_catalog.OC Certificate of Occupancy: Change of use or new construction; a bakery replacing a prior bakery is not a change of use.
permit_catalog.SUP Special Use Permit: Uses listed as special in the zoning district.

state.zoning_note: Zoning Code 19.40 (Downtown Mixed-Use): total wall sign area may not exceed 1.5 sq ft per linear foot of building frontage; internally illuminated signs must be switched off by 11:00 pm; no flashing or animated signs. Blade signs may project up to 4 ft over the sidewalk with 8 ft clearance and a ROW permit. Channel letters mounted flush to the facade do not project.

state.counter_hours: Permit Center: Mon-Thu 8:00-4:30, closed Fridays. Historic Commission staff available Tuesdays.

statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(a): A veteran with a service-connected disability rating of 100%, or rated as individually unemployable, is exempt from property tax on the veteran's primary residence.
statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(b): The exemption continues for the unremarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran. It ends if the surviving spouse remarries. If that later marriage ends by divorce or death, eligibility is restored upon new application.
statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(c): The veteran's disability status must be documented by a current VA benefit summary letter.
statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(d): Only one exemption under this section per property.
statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(e): The applicant must occupy the property as a primary residence on the assessment date and file an occupancy affidavit with each new application.
statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(f): Applications are filed with the assessor of the town where the property is located. Late filing results in the exemption beginning with the following assessment year.

era_rules.ERA 1 Eligibility: Renter households with income at or below 50% of area median income (system field income_band) that have experienced a financial hardship during the current lease year.
era_rules.ERA 2 Documentation: Hardship may be documented by a termination letter, a reduced-hours statement from the employer, medical bills, or a signed self-attestation when documents are unavailable.
era_rules.ERA 3 Priority: Households with a court-filed eviction or a written notice to vacate are processed first.
era_rules.ERA 4 Exclusions: Assistance may not be paid for any month already covered by ERA. Households living in public housing are excluded. Housing Choice Voucher holders are eligible only for the tenant's share of rent.
era_rules.ERA 5 Landlord participation: Payments go to the landlord, who must sign the landlord agreement. If the landlord refuses to sign or does not respond after two contact attempts, payment may be made to the tenant.
era_rules.ERA 6 Maximum: Up to 12 months of assistance per household across all ERA applications, including arrears and future rent.
era_rules.ERA 7 Utilities: Utility arrears may be included only when the tenant pays the utility directly and provides a current bill.
era_rules.ERA 8 Program integrity: Staff must refer suspected false statements to the Program Integrity Unit and must not deny on suspicion alone.

state.protection_rule: Tariff Rule 22.6 (Elderly and Minor Households). The utility shall not disconnect residential service for nonpayment where every adult resident of the premises is 65 or older, or where the only other residents are under 18. This protection does not apply if the utility has offered a deferred payment arrangement in writing and the customer has declined it in writing or failed to respond to two written offers. The customer must notify the utility of the household composition; the utility may rely on the most recent notification. Rule 22.7: before any disconnection of a protected-class customer, a field visit must be attempted.
state.field_visit_procedure: Field visits for protected-class customers are scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The representative must attempt to speak with the customer in person and leave a door hanger with the payment-plan phone number if no one answers.
state.agent_script: When a customer reports a household change, ask for the approximate date of the change and update the premise record. No documentation is required unless fraud is suspected.

rule.MED-1: A residential customer may obtain a 60-day hold on disconnection by filing a Medical Certification Form (MCF) completed by a licensed physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner, certifying that a household member has a serious medical condition or depends on electrically powered medical equipment.
rule.MED-2: The MCF must be signed and dated by the certifier and include the certifier's license number. Unsigned or incomplete forms are returned; the hold begins on the date a complete form is received.
rule.MED-3: While a hold is in effect, the customer should contact the utility about a payment arrangement. Failure to do so does not end the hold.
rule.MED-4: A customer may renew certification once per calendar year.
rule.MED-5: Faxed and portal-uploaded forms are accepted. Photos of forms are accepted if all fields are legible.
rule.MED-6: Collections must release any field disconnect order within one business day of receiving a complete MCF.
rule.MED-7: Medical information on the MCF is confidential and may be used only to administer the hold.

state.collections_procedure: Field disconnect orders are released to crews at 07:00 each business day for that day's route; orders not recalled by 06:30 are worked. Hold periods are counted in calendar days from the receipt date recorded in the document log.
